newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo says he's ready to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo says he's ready to stand trial.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said Monday he was ready to stand trial to prove his charges that a Supreme Court judge was corrupt.

"I will present proof that my remarks were truthful and I will demonstrate that it was not my intention to insult," he told a local radio station two days after a federal judge said he should stand trial for slandering a top court magistrate.

Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco said Saturday that Cavallo, the architect of Argentina's return to economic growth and currency stability, will stand trial on December 18 for slandering Supreme Court Judge Augusto Belluscio.
Cavallo in 1993 called Belluscio and another judge "corrupt" and said they had probably stolen missing court files in a case in which they ruled against the Central Bank.

Both sued and the other judge accepted a retraction, while Belluscio described the ex-minister's lukewarm recanting as too little too late and demanded he stand trial. Bagnasco then ruled that Cavallo had shown no sign of repentance.
Far from repentant, the former minister, who last July was sacked by President Carlos Menem after six years in the cabinet, was defiant on Monday.
"It makes no sense for me to apologize when my cause is just and it makes no sense for me to retract when what I said was true," he said.
Cavallo has whipped up a political storm since his sacking by accusing two senior cabinet ministers and Menem's top aide of blocking corruption investigations and manipulating judges.
They deny the charges and one is suing him.
